name: Subhashree Lenka/ ଶୁଭଶ୍ରୀ ଲେଙ୍କା

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Subhashree Lenka writes poetry in Odia, with work also available in translation. Her collections include “ସେଇ ଶବ୍ଦମାନେ”, published by Paschima Publication in 2018. Her poems have appeared in English in Sahitya Akademi’s Indian Literature, and her writing has been studied in teaching material from Shailabala Women’s Autonomous College.

The poems gathered here confront power and the suffering it can conceal. “ବୁଲଡ଼ୋଜର” questions the people who turn a machine into an emblem of justice, reminding them of its capacity to destroy. “ମଉନ ମଣିପୁର” centres women’s humiliation and displacement, insisting on shared grief across communities and calling silence to account. These are urgent public addresses, shaped by questions rather than reassurance.

poems_read.title: ବୁଲଡ଼ୋଜର
poems_read.coverage: Full original Odia poem, including separated final address.
poems_read.basis: Machine used for land, roads, minerals and demolition; neither distinctions nor moral agency; justice named after its force, political masters and Aladdin image, building/destruction and warning to controller.

poems_read.title: ମଉନ ମଣିପୁର
poems_read.coverage: Both complete original Odia stanzas read.
poems_read.basis: Speaker absent from violence yet ethically implicated; women publicly humiliated, homes burned, cultural dance/clothing displaced by grief, Kuki/Meitei suffering shared, demand for historical accountability. No named perpetrator or author affiliation inferred.
